sources.entry: FiScript - Execute custom scripts from the MacOS context menu (CTRL+click) in Finder.

summary.one_liner: FiScript is a macOS app that lets you run custom scripts on selected files or folders from the Finder right-click (CTRL+click) context menu.
summary.what_it_does: FiScript adds script execution to the Finder context menu on macOS. It runs user-defined scripts against the files or folders you select in Finder. The README says it is open source under the MIT License. Install is via Homebrew Cask (the command is truncated in the README) or by downloading the app manually. The README also says that scripts can be shared with others via the repository, but it does not describe how scripts are written or configured.
use_cases: run custom scripts on files from Finder
add script actions to the Mac context menu
batch process selected files or folders
how_to_run: brew cask install (Homebrew Cask; package name not shown in README)
Or manually: download, open, and drag FiScript to the Applications folder
Allow FiScript in Preferences > Security & Privacy > General since the app is not signed
Accept the 'FiScript Helper' prompt if it appears
If it does not show in the Finder menu, relaunch Finder (Apple Logo > Force Quit > Finder > Relaunch)
notable: Runs custom scripts from the Finder CTRL+click context menu
Open source under the MIT License
Users can share their own scripts with others through the repository
caveats: App is not code-signed, so it must be allowed manually in Security & Privacy settings
May need a Finder restart before it appears in the menu
keywords: add scripts to right click menu mac
